{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.",
    "If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next period.",
    "After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged flat or downward trend — adjust downward by 3–8% in next 3–5 days.",
    "When sentiment is flat (all 0.00), model shows no mean reversion signal; force a slight upward bias (1–3%) to account for latent volatility.",
    "If model forecast is trending upward but true outcome shows downward correction, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid over-optimism.",
    "If model forecast is flat or slightly downward but true outcome shows upward spike, increase forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 days to capture sentiment-driven momentum.",
    "In cases where true outcome deviates >10% from model, check sentiment history for recent reversal — if sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model may be lagging; adjust forecast downward by 5–10% for next 3–5 days."
  ]
}
